cataract: overall hazy or blurred appearance of the entire fundus image
reduced contrast and sharpness due to lens opacity
washed-out colors with dull optic disc and vessels
glare or scattered light artifacts near the center
partial obscuration of the macula and optic disc
lack of any discrete retinal lesions or hemorrhages
no signs of neovascularization or edema
image quality may vary depending on cataract severity
diabetic retinopathy: presence of microaneurysms appearing as small red dots
dot and blot retinal hemorrhages in posterior pole
hard exudates—yellowish deposits with sharp borders
cotton wool spots indicating localized ischemia
neovascularization on disc or elsewhere in advanced stages
macular edema causing thickening and loss of foveal reflex
retinal hemorrhages with irregular shapes and distribution
capillary dropout and poorly perfused areas
glaucoma: neuroretinal rim thinning, especially inferiorly and superiorly
notching of the optic disc rim
asymmetry of optic disc cupping between eyes
loss of retinal nerve fiber layer striations
constricted visual field zones in clinical correlation
normal macula and vessels unless coexisting conditions present
normal retina: well-defined optic disc with healthy cup-to-disc ratio (~0.3)
clear macular reflex with no edema or discoloration
intact vascular tree with no dilation, hemorrhage, or beading
visible foveal avascular zone at the center
sharp disc margins without notching or pallor
even illumination and clarity across the field
absence of any pathological signs or artifacts
